about: Values read by hand from documents in this directory that cannot be extracted by script (PDF). Each entry names the file, its SHA-256, the page and the sentence it was read from. `npm run reference` checks the file against the hash and copies the values into reference.json.

triple point of water.quote: the best estimate of the value of TTPW remains 273.16 K. [...] The standard uncertainty of TTPW is hence now u(TTPW) = 0.1 mK.

triple point of neon.quote: Table 1: T90 = 24.5561 K (Ne), T-T90 = -0.06 mK, u = 0.20 mK. The value is T90 plus the difference; 24.5561 K is the triple point of neon on the ITS-90.

triple point of argon.quote: Table 1: T90 = 83.8058 K (Ar), T-T90 = -4.21 mK, u = 0.15 mK. The value is T90 plus the difference; 83.8058 K is the triple point of argon on the ITS-90.

triple point of hydrogen.quote: Table 1: T90 = 13.8033 K (e-H2), T-T90 = 0.36 mK, u = 0.19 mK. The value is T90 plus the difference; 13.8033 K is the triple point of equilibrium hydrogen on the ITS-90.

triple-point pressure of water.quote: 4.2 Triple Point: "For the triple-point pressure, we recommend the value measured by Guildner et al. [17], which is (611.657 ± 0.010) Pa."

triple-point pressure of hydrogen.note: The table gives no uncertainty; taken as one unit in the last digit.

triple-point pressure of neon.note: The table gives no uncertainty; taken as the difference from the NIST Chemistry WebBook value, 43.370 kPa (nist-webbook-neon.html).

triple-point pressure of argon.note: The table gives no uncertainty; taken as the difference from the NIST Chemistry WebBook value, 68.900 kPa (nist-webbook-argon.html).

GM of the Sun.note: The fact sheet gives no uncertainty; taken as one unit in the last digit.

radius of the Sun.note: The fact sheet gives no uncertainty; taken as one unit in the last digit.

luminosity of the Sun.note: The fact sheet gives no uncertainty; taken as one unit in the last digit.

effective temperature of the Sun.note: The fact sheet gives no uncertainty; taken as one unit in the last digit.

helium per hydrogen atom in the Sun.quote: Photosphere Composition: Major elements: H - 90.965%, He - 8.889% (by number); the value is 8.889 / 90.965.
helium per hydrogen atom in the Sun.note: Helium in the photosphere is not measured directly but inferred; an uncertainty of 5 % is assumed.

GM of the Earth.note: The fact sheet gives no uncertainty; taken as one unit in the last digit.

semimajor axis of the Earth.note: The fact sheet gives no uncertainty; taken as one unit in the last digit.

sidereal year.quote: Orbital parameters: Sidereal orbit period (days) 365.256; the value is 365.256 × 86400 s.
sidereal year.note: The fact sheet gives no uncertainty; taken as one unit in the last digit.

temperature of the background radiation.quote: Abstract: "... a CMB background temperature of 2.72548±0.00057 K."

charge asymmetry of the long-lived neutr.note: AL is the difference between decays with a positron and with an electron, divided by their sum.

distance from the Sun to the Galactic ce.quote: "Solar distance from Galactic center R0 8.275 ± 0.009(stat.) ± 0.033(sys.) kpc"
distance from the Sun to the Galactic ce.note: The two uncertainties are combined in quadrature.

circular velocity at the Sun.quote: "circular velocity at R0 v0 or Θ0 233.4 ± 0.3(stat.) ± 8.0(sys.) km s−1"

mass of the Galactic centre.note: The uncertainty is taken as the difference from the 2019 value, 4.152 × 10^6 (gravity2019-r0.pdf, page 4), much larger than the statistical error.

Sun's motion toward the Galactic centre.quote: "we obtain (U, V, W)⊙ = (11.1+0.69 −0.75, 12.24+0.47 −0.47, 7.25+0.37 −0.36) km s−1, with additional systematic uncertainties ∼ (1, 2, 0.5) km s−1." The uncertainty is the larger statistical one and the systematic one, added in quadrature.

Sun's motion along the Galactic rotation.quote: "we obtain (U, V, W)⊙ = (11.1+0.69 −0.75, 12.24+0.47 −0.47, 7.25+0.37 −0.36) km s−1, with additional systematic uncertainties ∼ (1, 2, 0.5) km s−1." The uncertainty is the larger statistical one and the systematic one, added in quadrature.

Sun's motion toward the north Galactic p.quote: "we obtain (U, V, W)⊙ = (11.1+0.69 −0.75, 12.24+0.47 −0.47, 7.25+0.37 −0.36) km s−1, with additional systematic uncertainties ∼ (1, 2, 0.5) km s−1." The uncertainty is the larger statistical one and the systematic one, added in quadrature.

average adult body mass.quote: Table 1, row World: population 4630 (millions), average body mass 62.0 kg, biomass 287017 (thousand tonnes); for 2005. No uncertainty is given: measurements.ts adds a model uncertainty.

average height of the tallest adults.quote: "Dutch men, at 182.5 cm (180.6–184.5), the tallest people on the planet" (men born in 1996). The uncertainty is a quarter of the 95% credible interval.

average height of the shortest adults.quote: "Women born in 1996 are shortest in Guatemala, with an average height of 149.4 cm (148.0–150.8)". The uncertainty is a quarter of the 95% credible interval.

human body temperature.quote: "the standard for normal human body temperature of 37°C [...] (range: 36.2–37.5°C)" (Wunderlich) and "mean oral temperature to be 36.6°C" (Obermeyer et al. 2017). The value is the middle of the two means, the uncertainty half their difference.

DNA axial rise per base pair.quote: "The biologically predominant B-form of duplex DNA comprises a right-handed double helix containing two antiparallel sugar-phosphate chains [...] Between the base pairs of B-DNA there is an axial rise of 3.4 Å (0.34 nm) and a 34.5° twist angle". No uncertainty is given: measurements.ts adds a model uncertainty.

DNA twist per base pair.quote: The same sentence: "a 34.5° twist angle associated with every residue rotation". No uncertainty is given: measurements.ts adds a model uncertainty.
